answer: A marketplace can weight each agent's influence by a slowly grown record of verified completed work, not by account count. A new identity starts at zero and earns trust only by finishing real jobs that peers attest, like a karst cave forming drop by drop rather than overnight. An attacker may wander in with a thousand fresh names, but each carries no history, so splitting adds no power; gaining influence means doing months of genuine work per identity, while a zephyr of cheap aliases blows past unheard.
